course.title: Tailoring and Fashion Design
course.tagline: Cut, sew and finish clothes that fit beautifully, from measurements to a finished outfit.

days.title: Your Tools and Workspace
days.goal: Set up a sewing workspace and identify every basic tailoring tool.

video.title: Beginner Fashion Designing Course

steps: Clear a flat table at least 1m wide and set your machine on the left, iron on the right.
Lay out scissors, tape measure, pins, chalk, seam ripper and hand needles and name each one.
Thread your machine once slowly, following the numbered thread path in its manual.
Sew three straight lines on scrap cotton and check the stitch length.
days.task: Photograph your set-up workspace with every tool labelled on paper.
days.challenge: Sew a perfectly straight 30cm seam without the fabric drifting.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do before threading a sewing machine?
options: Raise the presser foot and follow the thread path
quiz.explain: Raising the presser foot opens the tension discs so the thread seats correctly.

quiz.q: Which tool is used to remove stitches?
quiz.explain: A seam ripper has a sharp point and blade made for cutting stitches without tearing fabric.

quiz.q: Why do you press seams as you sew?
options: It sets the stitches and gives a professional finish
quiz.explain: Pressing as you go sets stitches flat and keeps the garment shaping correctly.

days.title: Know Your Fabrics
days.goal: Tell cotton, Ankara, linen, chiffon and denim apart by look and feel.

video.title: Beginner Fashion Designing Course

steps: Collect five small fabric swatches from a market or old clothes.
Hold each up to the light and note which are sheer, stiff or stretchy.
Pull each swatch gently both ways to test stretch and to see which way the threads run (this is called the grain).
Write the name, feel and best use of each swatch on a card.
days.task: Label five swatches with fabric name and one garment each suits.
days.challenge: Identify an unknown fabric from a friend's wardrobe by feel alone.

quiz.q: How can you tell fabrics apart?
options: By the shop they came from.
quiz.explain: Tell cotton, Ankara, linen, chiffon and denim apart by look and feel.

quiz.q: What does it mean when a fabric is sheer?
options: You can see light through it.
quiz.explain: Hold each swatch up to the light and note which are sheer, stiff or stretchy.

quiz.q: What is the grain of a fabric?
quiz.explain: Pull each swatch gently both ways to test stretch and to see which way the threads run (this is called the grain).

days.title: Take Accurate Body Measurements
days.goal: Measure bust, waist, hip, shoulder and length correctly on a real person.

video.title: Beginner Fashion Designing Course

steps: Tie a ribbon around the natural waist so you can find it every time.
Measure bust, waist and hips snugly, keeping the tape level all round.
Record shoulder width, back length and sleeve length on a measurement sheet.
Repeat every measurement once and keep the second reading if it differs.
days.task: Complete a full measurement sheet for yourself or a willing model.
days.challenge: Measure someone in under five minutes with no errors on re-check.

quiz.q: Where do you tie a ribbon before you measure?
quiz.explain: Tie a ribbon around the natural waist so you can find it every time.

quiz.q: Which measurements do you take around the body?
quiz.explain: Measure bust, waist and hips snugly, keeping the tape level all round.

quiz.q: What should you do if your second measurement is different from the first?
quiz.explain: Repeat every measurement once and keep the second reading if it differs.

days.title: Pattern Paper and Marking Tools
days.goal: Prepare pattern paper and mark grainlines, notches and seam allowances correctly.

video.title: Pattern Making & Draping | Complete Fashion Design Tutorials for Beginners & Professionals

steps: Tape brown paper or newspaper sheets together into a 1m by 1m drafting surface.
Draw a straight arrow to show the grain (the direction the threads run) and a 90-degree cross line with a set square.
Mark 1.5cm of extra fabric for the seam (called the seam allowance) around a rectangle and cut it out cleanly.
Label the piece with its name, size, grainline and number of pieces to cut.
days.task: Draft and label one marked pattern piece with grainline and seam allowance.
days.challenge: Draw a perfect right angle and parallel grainline freehand with a ruler.

quiz.q: What is a grainline on a pattern piece?
options: An arrow showing the direction of the fabric grain
quiz.explain: The grainline arrow must run parallel to the selvedge so the garment hangs correctly.

quiz.q: How much extra fabric do you mark for the seam allowance?
quiz.explain: Mark 1.5cm of extra fabric for the seam (called the seam allowance) around a rectangle.

quiz.q: What should you write on a pattern piece?
options: Its name, size, grainline and number of pieces to cut.
quiz.explain: Label the piece with its name, size, grainline and number of pieces to cut.

days.title: Draft a Straight Skirt Block
days.goal: Draft a basic straight skirt pattern (called a block) from real waist and hip measurements.

video.title: Pattern Making & Draping | Complete Fashion Design Tutorials for Beginners & Professionals

steps: Divide your hip measurement by four and add 1cm of extra room (this extra room is called ease) for the quarter block.
Draw the waist, hip and hem lines on pattern paper using your measurements.
Shape the side seam with a gentle curve from hip to waist.
Add darts at the back waist, 1.5cm wide and 10cm long.
days.task: Finish a labelled straight skirt block on paper, ready to cut.
days.challenge: Draft the same block from a friend's measurements without help.

quiz.q: How do you work out the quarter block from your hip measurement?
options: Divide the hip by four and add 1cm of ease.
Use the hip number as it is.
quiz.explain: Divide your hip measurement by four and add 1cm of extra room (this extra room is called ease) for the quarter block.

quiz.q: How wide and long are the darts on the skirt block?
quiz.explain: Add darts at the back waist, 1.5cm wide and 10cm long.

quiz.q: Why add ease to a pattern block?
options: So the garment allows movement and breathing
quiz.explain: Ease is the extra room beyond body measurements that lets a garment move comfortably.

days.title: Reading a Commercial Pattern
days.goal: Read a shop-bought pattern envelope and cut the right size and pieces.

video.title: Pattern Making & Draping | Complete Fashion Design Tutorials for Beginners & Professionals

steps: Find the size chart on a pattern envelope and match it to your measurements.
Identify the cutting layout diagram for your fabric width.
Trace one pattern piece, transferring all notches and dots.
Check the finished garment measurements printed on the tissue.
days.task: Trace and label one full pattern piece from a commercial pattern.
days.challenge: Explain what every symbol on a pattern piece means to a friend.

quiz.q: What do you check first on a pattern envelope?
options: The size chart, to match it to your measurements.
quiz.explain: Find the size chart on a pattern envelope and match it to your measurements.

quiz.q: What does the cutting layout diagram show you?
options: How to place the pieces on your fabric width.
quiz.explain: Identify the cutting layout diagram for your fabric width.

quiz.q: What should you move onto the traced piece?
quiz.explain: Trace one pattern piece, transferring all notches and dots.

days.title: Project: Sew a Simple Straight Skirt
days.goal: Cut and sew a wearable straight skirt from your own block.

video.title: How to Draft A Bodice From Measurements

steps: Pin your skirt block to fabric, matching the grainline to the fabric grain.
Cut both front and back pieces plus a waistband, adding seam allowances.
Sew the side seams, insert the zip, then attach the waistband.
Hem the skirt evenly and press every seam flat.
days.task: Finish a straight skirt you can try on and wear.
days.challenge: Sew the skirt with no visible puckering at the waistband.

quiz.q: What do you pin to the fabric first when you sew the skirt?
options: Your skirt block, matching the grainline to the fabric grain.
quiz.explain: Pin your skirt block to fabric, matching the grainline to the fabric grain.

quiz.q: What do you sew after the side seams on the skirt?
options: The hem first, then the zip.
quiz.explain: Sew the side seams, insert the zip, then attach the waistband.

quiz.q: What is the last step before you try the skirt on?
options: Hem the skirt evenly and press every seam flat.
quiz.explain: Hem the skirt evenly and press every seam flat.

project.title: Sew a Simple Straight Skirt
project.brief: Cut and sew a straight skirt from your own drafted block, with a zip and waistband.
checks: Cut on grain with seam allowances

days.title: Machine Basics: Threading and Tension
days.goal: Thread any sewing machine correctly and fix skipped or loopy stitches.

video.title: How to Draft A Bodice From Measurements

steps: Re-thread the top thread and bobbin from scratch, step by step.
Sew a test line and inspect top and bottom for loops or tight puckers.
Adjust the tension dial one number at a time until both sides look even.
Clean lint from the bobbin area with a small brush.
days.task: Produce a test strip with balanced stitches on top and underneath.
days.challenge: Diagnose and fix a looping stitch problem in under five minutes.

quiz.q: What should you do first when your stitches look loopy?
options: Re-thread the top thread and bobbin from scratch.
quiz.explain: Re-thread the top thread and bobbin from scratch, step by step.

quiz.q: How should you change the tension dial?
options: Turn it all the way up at once.
Turn it all the way down at once.
One number at a time, until both sides look even.
quiz.explain: Adjust the tension dial one number at a time until both sides look even.

quiz.q: What should you clean from the bobbin area?
quiz.explain: Clean lint from the bobbin area with a small brush.

days.title: Seam Finishes That Last
days.goal: Sew plain, French and overlocked-style seams that do not fray.

video.title: How to Draft A Bodice From Measurements

steps: Sew a plain seam on cotton and press it open.
Sew the same seam as a French seam, which folds the cut (raw) edges inside so they cannot fray.
Finish a raw edge with a zigzag stitch close to the edge.
Compare all three seams after a firm tug and note which frays least.
days.task: Make a 15cm sample of each seam finish, labelled.
days.challenge: Sew a French seam on chiffon without the fabric slipping.

quiz.q: What is a French seam?
options: A seam that folds the raw edges inside so they cannot fray.
A seam on the outside only.
quiz.explain: Sew the same seam as a French seam, which folds the cut (raw) edges inside so they cannot fray.

quiz.q: How do you finish a raw edge so it does not fray?
options: With a zigzag stitch close to the edge.
By cutting it with plain scissors.
quiz.explain: Finish a raw edge with a zigzag stitch close to the edge.

quiz.q: How do you compare the three seam finishes?
options: Give each a firm tug and note which frays least.
Wash them and throw them away.
quiz.explain: Compare all three seams after a firm tug and note which frays least.

days.title: Cutting Fabric Accurately
days.goal: Lay out, pin and cut fabric on grain with clean, accurate edges.

video.title: Pattern Making • Cutting • Sewing | Complete Garment Tutorial | All Levels

steps: Fold the fabric so the finished edges (called selvedges) meet and the grain runs straight.
Pin pattern pieces with the grain arrow running the same way as the finished edge of the fabric (the selvedge).
Cut with long smooth strokes, keeping the scissors flat on the table.
Mark all notches with small snips and darts with chalk.
days.task: Cut a full skirt front and back accurately on grain.
days.challenge: Cut a slippery fabric without it shifting off the line.

quiz.q: What does "cut on grain" mean?
options: Cut with the grainline arrow parallel to the selvedge
quiz.explain: Cutting on grain keeps the garment hanging straight instead of twisting.

quiz.q: Why mark notches on cut pieces?
options: To match pieces correctly when sewing
quiz.explain: Notches are alignment marks that show which edges join and where.

quiz.q: What is a seam allowance?
options: The fabric left between the stitching line and the cut edge
quiz.explain: Seam allowance, usually 1.5cm, is the fabric between the stitch line and the raw edge.

days.title: Darts, Gathers and Pleats
days.goal: Shape flat fabric to the body with darts, gathers and knife pleats.

video.title: Pattern Making • Cutting • Sewing | Complete Garment Tutorial | All Levels

steps: Mark a waist dart on fabric and sew it from the wide end to a point.
Press the dart toward the centre back and check it lies flat.
Gather a 30cm strip by sewing two rows of long stitches and pulling the threads.
Fold and press three even knife pleats on a practice strip.
days.task: Make a sample strip showing one dart, one gather and one pleat.
days.challenge: Sew a dart that ends in a smooth point with no pucker.

quiz.q: How do you sew a waist dart?
options: From the point to the wide end.
From the wide end to a point.
quiz.explain: Mark a waist dart on fabric and sew it from the wide end to a point.

quiz.q: How do you gather a strip of fabric?
options: Sew two rows of long stitches and pull the threads.
quiz.explain: Gather a 30cm strip by sewing two rows of long stitches and pulling the threads.

quiz.q: How many knife pleats do you press on the practice strip?
quiz.explain: Fold and press three even knife pleats on a practice strip.

days.title: Necklines: Round, V and Square
days.goal: Cut and finish three neckline shapes cleanly with facings.

video.title: Pattern Making • Cutting • Sewing | Complete Garment Tutorial | All Levels

steps: Draw round, V and square necklines on paper and compare their depth.
Cut a facing (a shaped piece of fabric that finishes the neckline edge) for a round neckline and sew it right sides together.
Clip the curves, turn the facing inside and press it flat.
Topstitch 3mm from the edge to hold the facing in place.
days.task: Finish one round neckline with a facing that sits flat.
days.challenge: Cut a V-neck that meets in a sharp, clean point.

quiz.q: What is a facing?
options: A shaped piece of fabric that finishes the neckline edge.
quiz.explain: Cut a facing (a shaped piece of fabric that finishes the neckline edge) for a round neckline and sew it right sides together.

quiz.q: What should you do after sewing a facing to a round neckline?
options: Iron it with high heat only.
Clip the curves, turn it inside and press it flat.
quiz.explain: Clip the curves, turn the facing inside and press it flat.

quiz.q: How far from the edge do you topstitch the facing?
quiz.explain: Topstitch 3mm from the edge to hold the facing in place.

days.title: Sleeves: The Set-In Sleeve
days.goal: Set a sleeve into an armhole without puckers or twisting.

video.title: Beginner Sewing: Simple Dress from Rectangles and Elastic, No Pattern

steps: Measure the armhole curve and compare it with the curved top of the sleeve (called the sleeve cap).
Ease the sleeve cap with two rows of gathering stitches.
Pin the sleeve to the armhole, matching notches and the shoulder mark.
Sew slowly, easing the fullness in as you go, then press.
days.task: Set one sleeve into a practice bodice smoothly.
days.challenge: Set a sleeve with zero puckers on the first try.

quiz.q: What do you compare before you set a sleeve?
options: The armhole curve and the sleeve cap.
quiz.explain: Measure the armhole curve and compare it with the curved top of the sleeve (called the sleeve cap).

quiz.q: How do you ease the sleeve cap?
options: With two rows of gathering stitches.
quiz.explain: Ease the sleeve cap with two rows of gathering stitches.

quiz.q: What should you match when you pin the sleeve to the armhole?
options: The notches and the shoulder mark.
quiz.explain: Pin the sleeve to the armhole, matching notches and the shoulder mark.

days.title: Project: Sew a Fitted Bodice Top
days.goal: Make a fitted bodice top with darts, a neckline facing and a zip.

video.title: Beginner Sewing: Simple Dress from Rectangles and Elastic, No Pattern

steps: Cut the bodice front, back and facing from your drafted block.
Sew the darts, shoulder and side seams, then press them.
Attach the facing and insert an invisible zip at the back.
Hem the bottom evenly and try the top on for fit.
days.task: Finish a fitted bodice top that fits at bust, waist and shoulders.
days.challenge: Fit the top on a model and fix one fit issue on the spot.

quiz.q: What do you sew first on the bodice top?
options: The darts, shoulder and side seams, then press them.
quiz.explain: Sew the darts, shoulder and side seams, then press them.

quiz.q: Where does the invisible zip go on the bodice top?
quiz.explain: Attach the facing and insert an invisible zip at the back.

quiz.q: What should you check when you try the bodice top on?
options: The fit at bust, waist and shoulders.
quiz.explain: Finish a fitted bodice top that fits at bust, waist and shoulders.

project.title: Sew a Fitted Bodice Top
project.brief: Make a fitted bodice top with darts, a faced neckline and an invisible zip.
checks: Side seams match at the waist
Top fits at bust and waist

days.title: Zips: Invisible and Lapped
days.goal: Insert an invisible zip and a lapped zip neatly.

video.title: Beginner Sewing: Simple Dress from Rectangles and Elastic, No Pattern

steps: Press the seam where the zip will go and mark the zip length.
Pin the invisible zip face down on one side and stitch with a zipper foot.
Repeat on the other side and close the seam below the zip.
Insert a lapped zip on a practice piece, overlapping one side by 3mm.
days.task: Insert one invisible zip that disappears into the seam.
days.challenge: Insert a zip in under 15 minutes with no wavy fabric.

quiz.q: What should you do before you insert a zip?
options: Press the seam and mark the zip length.
quiz.explain: Press the seam where the zip will go and mark the zip length.

quiz.q: How do you sew an invisible zip?
options: Pin it face down on one side and stitch with a zipper foot.
Pin it and leave it loose.
quiz.explain: Pin the invisible zip face down on one side and stitch with a zipper foot.

quiz.q: How much does one side overlap on a lapped zip?
quiz.explain: Insert a lapped zip on a practice piece, overlapping one side by 3mm.

days.title: Buttons, Buttonholes and Hooks
days.goal: Sew strong buttons, machine buttonholes and hook-and-eye closures.

video.title: How to Hand Sew Like a Machine

steps: Mark button positions evenly on a shirt front, starting below the bust.
Sew a button with a thread shank so it sits above the fabric.
Make a machine buttonhole on scrap, then cut it open carefully.
Sew a hook and eye so the edges meet exactly without gaping.
days.task: Make a placket sample with two buttons and two buttonholes.
days.challenge: Sew a buttonhole on thick fabric without the machine jamming.

quiz.q: Where do you start marking button positions on a shirt front?
quiz.explain: Mark button positions evenly on a shirt front, starting below the bust.

quiz.q: Why sew a button with a thread shank?
options: So it sits above the fabric.
quiz.explain: Sew a button with a thread shank so it sits above the fabric.

quiz.q: What should you do after you make a machine buttonhole?
quiz.explain: Make a machine buttonhole on scrap, then cut it open carefully.

days.title: Dress Construction Order
days.goal: Plan the correct order for building a dress from pieces to finish.

video.title: How to Hand Sew Like a Machine

steps: List every step of making a simple dress, from cutting to hemming.
Sew darts and seams first, then join the bodice to the skirt.
Insert the zip before attaching the neckline facing.
Leave hemming and pressing until the very end.
days.task: Write a step-by-step build order for a dress and follow it on paper.
days.challenge: Reorder a jumbled set of dress-making steps correctly.

quiz.q: What do you sew first when you build a dress?
options: Darts and seams first, then join the bodice to the skirt.
quiz.explain: Sew darts and seams first, then join the bodice to the skirt.

quiz.q: When do you insert the zip when you build a dress?
options: Insert the zip before attaching the neckline facing.
quiz.explain: Insert the zip before attaching the neckline facing.

quiz.q: What do you leave until the very end when you build a dress?
quiz.explain: Leave hemming and pressing until the very end.

days.title: Lining a Bodice
days.goal: Line a bodice so the inside looks as clean as the outside.

video.title: How to Hand Sew Like a Machine

steps: Cut the lining pieces slightly smaller than the shell pieces.
Sew the lining bodice together exactly like the outer bodice.
Join lining and shell at the neckline, right sides together.
Turn, press and hand-stitch the lining to the zip tapes.
days.task: Line a practice bodice with no lining showing at the neckline.
days.challenge: Line a bodice so it hangs without pulling the outer fabric.

quiz.q: How should lining pieces compare in size to the shell pieces?
quiz.explain: Cut the lining pieces slightly smaller than the shell pieces.

quiz.q: Where do lining and shell join?
options: At the neckline, right sides together.
quiz.explain: Join lining and shell at the neckline, right sides together.

quiz.q: What should you hand-stitch the lining to?
quiz.explain: Turn, press and hand-stitch the lining to the zip tapes.

days.title: Choosing Styles for Body Shapes
days.goal: Match neckline, sleeve and skirt styles to different body shapes.

video.title: 2 DRESSES IN 1 VIDEO! Easy Patternless Girls' Dress Sewing Tutorial

steps: Sketch three body shapes and note where each carries width.
Pair each shape with a flattering neckline and skirt style.
Explain why an A-line skirt suits a pear shape.
Pick a style for a real client based on their measurements.
days.task: Write style recommendations for three different body shapes.
days.challenge: Style a full outfit for a client from measurements alone.

quiz.q: What should you note first when you sketch body shapes?
quiz.explain: Sketch three body shapes and note where each carries width.

quiz.q: What do you pair each body shape with?
options: A flattering neckline and skirt style.
quiz.explain: Pair each shape with a flattering neckline and skirt style.

quiz.q: What should you base a style pick for a real client on?
quiz.explain: Pick a style for a real client based on their measurements.

days.title: Working with Ankara and Prints
days.goal: Cut and match printed and Ankara fabrics so patterns line up.

video.title: 2 DRESSES IN 1 VIDEO! Easy Patternless Girls' Dress Sewing Tutorial

steps: Identify the repeat in an Ankara print and mark it with pins.
Cut two matching pieces so the motif lines up at the side seam.
Match a stripe or check across a centre seam.
Press Ankara on the wrong side to protect the print.
days.task: Cut and sew a seam where the print matches across it.
days.challenge: Match a bold print across a bodice and skirt join.

quiz.q: What should you do with the repeat in an Ankara print?
options: Identify it and mark it with pins.
quiz.explain: Identify the repeat in an Ankara print and mark it with pins.

quiz.q: How do you cut two matching pieces in Ankara?
options: So the motif lines up at the side seam.
quiz.explain: Cut two matching pieces so the motif lines up at the side seam.

quiz.q: Which side should you press Ankara on?
options: The right side with high heat.
The wrong side, to protect the print.
quiz.explain: Press Ankara on the wrong side to protect the print.

days.title: Project: Sew a Complete Simple Dress
days.goal: Sew a complete dress with bodice, skirt, zip and finished hem.

video.title: 2 DRESSES IN 1 VIDEO! Easy Patternless Girls' Dress Sewing Tutorial

steps: Cut bodice and skirt pieces from one fabric, matching prints at the waist.
Assemble the bodice, attach the skirt, then insert the zip.
Finish the neckline with a facing and the armholes cleanly.
Hem, press and try the dress on, noting any fit fixes.
days.task: Finish a complete dress, pressed and ready to wear.
days.challenge: Complete the dress with no unfinished raw edges inside.

quiz.q: What do you do first when you sew the complete dress?
options: Cut bodice and skirt pieces from one fabric, matching prints at the waist.
quiz.explain: Cut bodice and skirt pieces from one fabric, matching prints at the waist.

quiz.q: What comes after you attach the skirt to the bodice?
quiz.explain: Assemble the bodice, attach the skirt, then insert the zip.

quiz.q: What should you note when you try the dress on?
options: The price of the fabric only.
The colour of the thread only.
quiz.explain: Hem, press and try the dress on, noting any fit fixes.

project.title: Sew a Complete Simple Dress
project.brief: Build a full dress: bodice, skirt, zip, facing and hem, pressed and wearable.

days.title: Sew with the Simple Turn-Through Method
days.goal: Make a neat flat item using the simple sew-turn-topstitch method.

video.title: One Simple Technique = Countless Easy Sewing Projects | Beginner Friendly

steps: Place two pieces of fabric right sides together and pin them.
Sew all round the edge, leaving a 10cm gap on one side.
Turn the piece right side out through the gap and poke the corners out gently.
Press it flat, tuck the gap edges in, and topstitch close to the edge.
days.task: Make a small flat item (a placemat or cushion cover) with the turn-through method.
days.challenge: Make the same item in a second fabric without looking at the video.

quiz.q: What is the simple turn-through technique?
options: Sewing two pieces right sides together, leaving a gap, then turning them out
quiz.explain: You sew around the edge, leave a gap, turn the piece right side out and topstitch it closed.

quiz.q: Why leave a gap when you sew around the piece?
options: So you can turn the fabric right side out through it
quiz.explain: The gap is the opening you pull the fabric through to turn it the right way round.

quiz.q: What should you do after turning the piece right side out?
options: Press it flat and topstitch around the edge
quiz.explain: Pressing flat and topstitching closes the gap and gives a neat, strong edge.

days.title: Fitting and Common Fit Fixes
days.goal: Diagnose pulling, gaping and sagging, and fix each one.

video.title: One Simple Technique = Countless Easy Sewing Projects | Beginner Friendly

steps: Try a garment on inside out and pin out the excess at the side seams.
Fix a gaping neckline by taking in the shoulder seam.
Fix a tight bust by letting out the side seams.
Fix a sagging back by shortening the back waist.
days.task: Fit a garment on a model and correct two fit problems.
days.challenge: Fix a gaping armhole without remaking the sleeve.

quiz.q: How do you try a garment on to find fit problems?
options: Right side out with no pins.
Inside out, then pin out the excess at the side seams.
quiz.explain: Try a garment on inside out and pin out the excess at the side seams.

quiz.q: How do you fix a gaping neckline?
quiz.explain: Fix a gaping neckline by taking in the shoulder seam.

quiz.q: How do you fix a tight bust?
quiz.explain: Fix a tight bust by letting out the side seams.

days.title: Alterations: Taking In and Letting Out
days.goal: Alter ready-made clothes to fit a customer properly.

video.title: One Simple Technique = Countless Easy Sewing Projects | Beginner Friendly

steps: Take in a shirt at the side seams by 2cm on each side.
Shorten a pair of trousers keeping the original hem look.
Let out a skirt waist by moving the zip and waistband.
Taper a dress from the waist down for a slimmer fit.
days.task: Alter one ready-made garment to fit its owner.
days.challenge: Take in a garment and keep both side seams even.

quiz.q: How much do you take in a shirt at each side seam?
quiz.explain: Take in a shirt at the side seams by 2cm on each side.

quiz.q: How do you let out a skirt waist?
quiz.explain: Let out a skirt waist by moving the zip and waistband.

quiz.q: How do you taper a dress for a slimmer fit?
options: Taper it from the waist down.
Taper it from the hem up.
quiz.explain: Taper a dress from the waist down for a slimmer fit.

days.title: Custom Fit Adjustments
days.goal: Adjust a block for a full bust, narrow shoulder or long torso.

video.title: How to Draft a Custom Fit Bodice Pattern

steps: Compare a client's measurements with the standard block.
Add a full-bust adjustment by slashing and spreading the front pattern.
Shorten a shoulder seam for a narrow-shouldered client.
Lengthen the bodice for a long torso, adding at the waist line.
days.task: Adjust a bodice block for one real body difference.
days.challenge: Draft a block that fits a client with two different adjustments.

quiz.q: How do you draft a custom fit bodice?
options: Use a standard size and hope
Draft from the wearer's own measurements
quiz.explain: A custom fit block starts from real body measurements, not a standard size chart.

quiz.q: What is a full bust adjustment?
options: Adding room across the bust without changing the shoulders
quiz.explain: A full bust adjustment slashes and spreads the front pattern to add bust room only.

quiz.q: Why fit a toile before cutting good fabric?
options: To test the fit cheaply and fix errors before cutting expensive cloth
quiz.explain: A toile in cheap fabric catches fit mistakes before they cost good fabric.

days.title: Pressing and Professional Finishing
days.goal: Press seams, hems and garments to a shop-quality finish.

video.title: How to Draft a Custom Fit Bodice Pattern

steps: Press every seam as you sew, never waiting until the end.
Use a pressing cloth on Ankara and delicate fabrics.
Press darts toward the centre and hems upward from the inside.
Hang the finished garment for 30 minutes before the final check.
days.task: Press a finished garment to a shop-ready standard.
days.challenge: Remove a shine mark from pressing without damaging fabric.

quiz.q: When should you press seams?
options: As you sew, never waiting until the end.
quiz.explain: Press every seam as you sew, never waiting until the end.

quiz.q: What should you use when you press Ankara and delicate fabrics?
options: A flat iron with no cloth.
quiz.explain: Use a pressing cloth on Ankara and delicate fabrics.

quiz.q: Which way do you press darts?
quiz.explain: Press darts toward the centre and hems upward from the inside.

days.title: Costing and Pricing Your Work
days.goal: Price a garment from fabric, time and profit so the hustle pays.

video.title: How to Draft a Custom Fit Bodice Pattern

steps: Add up fabric, thread, zip and lining costs for one dress.
Time yourself sewing it and value your hours at a fair rate.
Add 20 percent profit and round to a clean selling price.
Compare your price with two tailors in your area.
days.task: Produce a written price for one dress with the full costing shown.
days.challenge: Price a rush-order dress fairly for a same-week deadline.

quiz.q: What costs do you add up for one dress?
quiz.explain: Add up fabric, thread, zip and lining costs for one dress.

quiz.q: How much profit do you add to the cost?
quiz.explain: Add 20 percent profit and round to a clean selling price.

quiz.q: What should you compare your price with?
quiz.explain: Compare your price with two tailors in your area.

days.title: Photographing Garments and Taking Orders
days.goal: Present finished work and take clear, paid orders from customers.

video.title: Sure Fit Designs Introduction

steps: Photograph a garment on a hanger against a plain wall in daylight.
Take front, back and detail shots plus one worn shot.
Write an order form: style, fabric, measurements, price and date.
Ask for a 50 percent deposit before cutting any fabric.
days.task: Create an order form and a three-photo set for one garment.
days.challenge: Get a paying order using only photos of your past work.

quiz.q: How should you photograph a garment for a customer?
options: On the floor in the dark.
On a hanger against a plain wall in daylight.
quiz.explain: Photograph a garment on a hanger against a plain wall in daylight.

quiz.q: What should your order form list?
options: Style, fabric, measurements, price and date.
quiz.explain: Write an order form: style, fabric, measurements, price and date.

quiz.q: Why keep a client measurement book?
options: So repeat orders are fast and consistent
quiz.explain: Saved measurements mean the next order starts from correct numbers, not a fresh measuring session.

days.title: Capstone Planning
days.goal: Choose your capstone outfit, fabric and schedule for the final two days.

video.title: Sure Fit Designs Introduction

steps: Pick a two-piece outfit or dress that shows off your best skills.
Buy or choose the fabric and all notions today.
Cut every piece and label them in build order.
Write a two-day build plan with time for fitting and pressing.
days.task: Have all capstone pieces cut, labelled and ready to sew.
days.challenge: Plan a capstone outfit that uses at least three skills from the month.

quiz.q: What should your capstone outfit show off?

quiz.q: What should you buy or choose today for the capstone?

quiz.q: What should you write for the final two days?
options: A two-day build plan with time for fitting and pressing.

Fit it on the wearer and fix any issue before hemming.
Press the finished outfit and photograph it front, back and detail.
Present it with your costing sheet and a care note for the wearer.

options: Sew the outfit following your build plan, pressing as you go.

options: Pressing and a final fit check

capstone.title: Sew a Complete Two-Piece Outfit
capstone.brief: Design, cut and sew a complete two-piece outfit (top and skirt, or a dress with a jacket) for a real wearer, fitted, pressed and presented with a costing sheet.
checks: Outfit designed and cut from your own measurements or a client's
Bodice or top fits at bust, waist and shoulders
Skirt or second piece fits and matches the top
Zip, facing and hems finished cleanly with no raw edges
Garment pressed to a shop-ready finish
Photos taken: front, back and detail
Costing sheet shows fabric, notions, time and selling price
deliverables: Finished two-piece outfit, pressed and wearable
Three photos: front, back and detail
Short care note for the wearer
